title: Whether Edison should sing
summary: Dance suggests instrumentalists make good singers; Edison says he will try but can't remember lyrics.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: You never sang, did you?
No, no.
Did you have------ ?
A lot of people often asked me why I don't, you know?
Well, I mean --
Why I don't. Everybody else is doing it. I think I'll try it on something, you know?
Yeah. I was wondering, you know, because
you don't have to be -- have the greatest voice or anything.
That's for sure.
But -- well, I didn't mean you, but I mean, you know, there's a thing that all those guys that used to sing with Lunceford, like Joe Thomas, Willie Smith.
Yeah, yeah.
Even Ray Nance and Trummy Young.
You know, the thing is that a musician, he may not have a voice, but he knows how to phrase.
He knows where to leave out and what to put in, you know?
That's it. You know, it can be--
Oh, I'm going to try it, I'm going to try it.
It just depends where you are. Some places, you know, it adds a little variety.
Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. It breaks the monotony, too.
Yeah.
Well, I'm going to try it. But I can't ever remember the words to a song, you know?
(Laughter.)
You just scat.
Yeah, that's how Louie, Pops started.
Sure.
But I just can't seem to remember the words to everything.
You have to pick songs that --
Yeah, songs that are not too full of words, and I can remember what's going on, you know?
